title: Final Paper-Ready Results and Visualization Package

key_findings.Finding: M2 achieved the highest DDI Accuracy and Balanced Accuracy.
key_findings.Interpretation: Supported by the verified external evaluation.

key_findings.Finding: M2 + M3 achieved the highest DDI Macro-F1.
key_findings.Interpretation: Supported, but prediction coverage was only 41.90%.

key_findings.Finding: M3 produced the strongest R3 representation-bias reduction.
key_findings.Evidence: R3 probe BA decreased from 60.42% to 46.03%.

key_findings.Finding: M2 + M3 retained substantial R3 reduction while improving DDI Macro-F1.
key_findings.Interpretation: Useful combined result, but external prediction coverage limits confidence.

key_findings.Finding: Performance decreased substantially when moving from Fitzpatrick17k to DDI.
key_findings.Evidence: Observed negative generalization gaps for available Baseline and M2 metrics.

key_findings.Finding: DDI contains substantial out-of-space predictions under the harmonized label space.
key_findings.Evidence: M2 + M3 mapped 41.90% of predictions; 122/210 were out-of-space.
key_findings.Interpretation: External metrics must be interpreted cautiously.

limitations.Limitation: Fitzpatrick17k and DDI use different disease label spaces.
DDI evaluation uses a harmonized 14-class space rather than the full 114-class space.
M2 + M3 has only 41.90% prediction coverage on DDI.
122 of 210 DDI predictions are outside the harmonized prediction space.
Complete internal Fitzpatrick17k performance records are not available for M3 and M2 + M3.
Fairness metrics capture different aspects of disparity and may move in different directions.
Public-dataset evaluation does not establish clinical deployment readiness.
